column1: # The first hours (First hours worker, 11-05: pick up a rock, knap flint, lash a stone axe). Tiles for small box models on the ground. BLOCK_LIKE: stone,log_oak,gravel

column3: flint_nodule|cube|Flint as a block tile: a lumpy chalky white-cream rind (#b8b2a2 #d4cebe #e8e4d8) covering most of the square with knobbly shading, and two or three places where it is broken off showing smooth glassy near-black flint (#141418 #24242a #3a3a44) with a pale ripple, light from the top left, seamless
column4: fallen_branch|log|A fallen dead branch's bark: weathered grey-brown bark (#3a3430 #4e463e #625a50 #7a7062 #948a7a), dry and cracked lengthwise, a few lighter bare patches where the bark has flaked off showing silvery grey wood (#a8a294), a little pale green-grey lichen, the grain running top to bottom, seamless

column1: # Slices 2-3 (Ronald: "Fire bed + bow drill"). The fire bed's sticks are thin crossed boxes on the ground. BLOCK_LIKE: fallen_branch,tallgrass

column3: fire_bed|cube|A fire bed's material for thin stick boxes: weathered grey-brown deadwood sticks (#4a423a #5e544a #766a5c #8e806e #a6987e) lying lengthwise across the square, with tufts and strands of pale dry grass and fibre tinder (#b8a87a #ccbc8c #e0d4a8) tangled between and over them, a few dark charred flecks, seamless

column3: campfire_laid_top|face|The attached campfire's top EXACTLY, the same stone ring and the same crossed logs in the same places, but cold and unlit: no flames, no glow, no embers; the centre where the fire was holds a small heap of pale dry tinder (#c8b88a #dccc9c) and thin kindling sticks (#6a5e52 #8a7c6c), the logs' bark plain grey-brown, the stones their own grey-green
column4: campfire_laid_side|face|The attached campfire's side EXACTLY, the same logs lying across and the same stones below, in the same places, but cold and unlit: no flames, no glow; a few thin kindling sticks and a wisp of pale dry tinder poke up between the logs where the flames were, the same dark background above
